edges.notes: systemd targets Linux; other OS ports are non-mainline for this package scope.
Often coexists on container hosts for host services.
kubelet/node services commonly supervised by systemd on Linux nodes; not a hard universal dependency.
Same project family; composed with PID 1 on typical systemd-based OS images.
systemd ukify builds UKI artifacts per systemd.ukify(1).
PID 1 and related daemons load and interpret unit files per systemd.unit(5) and service-specific manuals.
Portable services and portablectl are documented systemd features for attaching portable OS-tree images.
systemd-sysext merges system extension images into configured hierarchies as part of the systemd suite.
systemd-confext merges configuration extension images into /etc-class hierarchies as part of the systemd suite.
Debian stable uses systemd as the default init system, running systemd as PID 1 on default installs.
Ubuntu uses systemd as the default init and service manager, running systemd as PID 1 on default installs.
Fedora uses systemd as the default init and service manager, running systemd as PID 1 on default installs.
RHEL uses systemd as the default init and service manager, running systemd as PID 1 on default installs.
Rocky Linux uses systemd as the default init and service manager, running systemd as PID 1 on default installs.
AlmaLinux uses systemd as the default init and service manager, running systemd as PID 1 on default installs.
CentOS Stream uses systemd as the default init and service manager, running systemd as PID 1 on default installs.
Historical CentOS Linux used systemd as the default init and service manager on supported releases where systemd applied, running systemd as PID 1 on default installs.
